# Cleaning a home espresso machine

A clean espresso machine makes better coffee and lasts longer. Coffee oils build up on every part that touches the brew, and old oils taste stale and bitter. Water leaves minerals inside the boiler and the pipes, and those deposits slow the flow and change the brew temperature. A short routine after every session and a deeper clean every few weeks keep both problems away.

## After every session

Run a short flush of hot water through the group head to rinse away loose grounds. Knock the spent puck into the bin, rinse the basket and wipe the portafilter dry with a cloth. Wipe the steam wand straight after you steam milk, then open the valve for a second to clear the milk that was pulled back inside the tip. Milk dries fast and sets hard, so this small step saves a lot of scrubbing later.

Empty the drip tray before it fills to the top. A full tray spills when you lift it and can smell sour by the next morning.

## Every week

Backflush the group head with a blind basket and a spoon of espresso machine cleaner. Lock the portafilter in, run the pump for ten seconds, stop it, and repeat five times. Then repeat the cycle with plain water to rinse the cleaner out. Soak the basket and the portafilter head in hot water with a little cleaner while you do this, and scrub the shower screen with a soft brush.

Check the group gasket while you are there. A gasket that feels hard or cracked lets water leak around the portafilter and should be replaced.

## Every month

Descale the machine if your water is hard. Follow the maker's guide for your model, since some boilers need a specific product and a specific cycle. Fill the tank with the descaling solution, run it through the group head and the steam wand in short bursts, wait for the time on the label, and then flush the whole system with two full tanks of fresh water.

## Keeping the water soft

The best way to cut the descaling work is to start with soft water. A filter jug or an inline filter removes much of the hardness. Test strips from a pet shop or a pool shop tell you how hard your tap water is, and the result helps you choose how often to descale. Store the strips in a dry drawer so they stay accurate.
